summary:
Allwork.Space reports, citing the Financial Times, that some Revolut subscribers have lost WeWork access across parts of Europe after WeWork sought higher fees for the partnership. Affected locations span Paris, Brussels, Milan, London, Edinburgh, Dublin and Prague; in Brussels, Edinburgh and Milan subscribers reportedly have no remaining WeWork access. Paris was removed even as Revolut prepares to open a new European headquarters there.

Rather than scrapping the benefit or passing the full cost increase to subscribers, the two companies negotiated a new arrangement effective at the start of August. Under it, eligible Revolut customers can access roughly 265 WeWork locations globally, more than half of them in the U.S.

WeWork day passes have been a feature of Revolut's higher-tier plans: the GBP 55 per month Ultra plan includes three one-day passes monthly, and the GBP 14.99 per month Metal plan includes one. The perk fits Revolut's approach of bundling third-party services, alongside gym, dating app and media benefits, into paid memberships. Revolut reported more than GBP 700 million in subscription revenue in 2025, up nearly 70% year over year.

WeWork attributed the change to economic conditions plus increased occupancy and demand at some locations, and said Revolut remains a partner whose customers will still have access to flexible workspace across its global network. Revolut said individual benefit availability can change but that it remains committed to premium workspace and lifestyle benefits.

The piece frames the renegotiation as a broader warning: when demand for physical workspace rises, the economics of bundled coworking access as an employee or customer perk can shift quickly, leaving perk providers renegotiating or narrowing coverage. It is primarily a flexible workspace and coworking market story rather than a workplace operations or policy story.
